openings.claim: Use the known strap separation-retention function alone: two removable fabric straps across the hatch carry tension to padded, bolted paired-strip rim clamps. No spacer function is proposed.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from an ordinary cord lash to fabric straps attached to removable strip clamps. Release and move the entire assembly beside the trough for inspection; recover all components. Clamp attachment, strap reach and unobstructed removal remain unproved.
openings.prediction: If balanced strap tension retains the hatch without reproducing the opposite-corner lift, it may also resist sideways motion through existing contact friction. Against a cord lash on the same anchors, compare marked displacement, corner lift, release time and visible seal damage. Wider strap contact might reduce concentrated loading; superiority and adequate friction are uncertain.
openings.probe: First check actual rim access, strap reach, reversible padded clamping and clear removal using supplied parts. Stop if these fail or damage appears. Fabricate within ninety minutes. Allocate ten closure/pull trials to the strap configuration, checking position, 20 N resistance, reopening time and seal after every cycle; use the right-contact card on trial ten. Allocate two trials to the ordinary cord rival, one normal and one disturbed. Complete observations within twenty minutes; count every closure/pull toward twelve. The rival receives only an exploratory comparison, not ten-cycle qualification.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits padded reversible clamps, which must be established rather than assumed.
The supplied straps reach and can be secured and released with supplied bolts; cord length suffices for the rival and recoverability.

Defeat conditions include insufficient reach or anchor capacity, corner lift, movement beyond 1 mm, failure under 20 N, reopening beyond 30 seconds, obstruction or new seal tears. Stop caps do not establish feasibility.

assessment: This is a bounded probe, not a deployment claim. Preserve the existing hatch, rim and seal without drilling, cutting, gluing or permanent deformation. All outcomes remain required after ten cycles and the disturbed final closure; only seal-contact continuity is exempted. Unknown geometry and retention capacity prevent a preserves verdict.
